heuristics: H1: the class walk on H/mu6 (H the 2^20-th powers in Z_r^*, 64 multiplicative steps in H) behaves as a random mapping on the M = (r-1)/(6*2^20) classes, so S tame and wild points give a tame-wild collision with probability 1 - exp(-S^2/(4M)).

H2: distinguished-point detection adds at most 2^90 steps per trail, and failures to reach a distinguished point within the 2^100-step cap and in-trail cycles are negligible; all such steps are charged.
H3: Callgrind instruction counts of the step's non-addition work on blst (2703.56 per step over 256 differenced steps) represent per-step work; 2800 instructions are charged.
limitations: H1 is an unproved standard heuristic; it is tested only on a toy generic group with up to 38-bit order.
The model success is 0.451188 at S = 2*sqrt(0.6*M); the claimed lower bound is 0.40, and pooled toy success at that budget is 0.416 over 1210 trials.
Analytic production cost; no production-size execution.
Peak memory is about 10 GB (distinguished-point table and window-16 comb tables); larger windows lower the score at much larger memory.
The 16 comb additions per step are charged as reference units; the measured kernel covers the remaining step work, plus an allowance of about 100 instructions for loop and trail bookkeeping.
